notes: Claude built a Video.js 10 (beta-23) player by directly reading the installed TypeScript declarations in node_modules before writing any code. Every claimed API has been verified against the published @videojs/react@10.0.0-beta.23 and @videojs/core@10.0.0-beta.23 packages: the imports (createPlayer, useComposedRefs, useMediaAttach, BufferingIndicator, CaptionsButton, Controls, FullscreenButton, Gesture, Hotkey, MuteButton, PiPButton, PlayButton, PlaybackRateButton, Poster, SeekButton, Slider, Time, TimeSlider, VolumeSlider) are real exports of @videojs/react; videoFeatures is a real export of @videojs/react/video; the side-effect import @videojs/html/media/hls-video matches the package's ./media/* export. The compound part accessors (Controls.Root, TimeSlider.Root/Track/Buffer/Fill/Thumb, VolumeSlider.Root/Track/Fill/Thumb, Time.Value) match the index.parts namespaces. Gesture and Hotkey props (type, action, pointer, region, keys, value) plus action names (togglePaused, toggleMuted, toggleFullscreen, toggleControls, seekStep, volumeStep) are all in the GestureActionName/HotkeyActionName unions. CSS custom properties (--media-slider-fill, --media-slider-buffer, --media-slider-pointer, --media-color-primary) and library class names (.media-default-skin, .media-default-skin--video, .media-controls, .media-button--mute, .media-button--fullscreen, .media-button--playback-rate, .media-button-group) and data attributes (data-paused, data-muted, data-volume-level, data-fullscreen, data-availability, data-visible, data-dragging) are all defined by the library. SeekButton's seconds prop and Poster's src/alt props are valid. No factual hallucinations were detected.
